crash_testing_methodology.approach: Disk-state injection at 9 discrete transaction boundaries (pre-intent, post-intent, corrupted temp file, pre-replace fsync, post-replace, pre-sqlite commit, mid-sqlite commit, repeated recovery, post-recovery replay)
crash_testing_methodology.realism: Accurate state-level simulation of power cut or abrupt process crash; verified deterministic recovery across all 9 boundaries.
crash_testing_methodology.finding: Tests use in-memory instance destruction (del broker) and ungraceful disk state recreation rather than OS SIGKILL. This is standard and reproducible for unit/integration suites without requiring external process supervision.

multiprocessing_methodology.approach: multiprocessing.get_context('spawn') with 4 concurrent OS processes competing for single order slot under file locks and SQLite busy timeout.
multiprocessing_methodology.realism: Genuine separate OS processes with independent memory spaces and Python interpreters.
multiprocessing_methodology.finding: Exactly 1 process won the slot; 3 failed cleanly; zero race conditions or database lock errors.

backup_restore_methodology.approach: sqlite3.Connection.backup() executed concurrently while 5 writer threads actively insert records.
backup_restore_methodology.realism: Online SQLite Backup API verified capturing uncheckpointed WAL frames without stopping writers.
backup_restore_methodology.finding: 100% of keys captured; isolated restore confirmed active open positions and replay deduplication intact.

combined_state_verification.finding: All tests assert financial state, fee accounting, and idempotency status jointly.
